Reports, slides and dashboards

Source: vignettes/articles/documents.Rmd
documents.Rmd

phwstyle gives whole documents the PHW look: the Ubuntu font, navy headings, the gradient header band, a cover page for PDFs and slides, and “Page x of y” footers. This page shows how to render a report, a slide deck or a dashboard from one document. The examples use made-up names. You choose a format once in the document’s YAML header, and the charts and tables inside follow the same style.

There are two routes. Use whichever your team already uses:

R Markdown (.Rmd) Quarto (.qmd)
Formats HTML, Word, PDF HTML, Word, PowerPoint, PDF (Typst or LaTeX), slides, dashboards
Setup None: the formats come with phwstyle Run use_phw_quarto() once in each project
Charts and flextables Styled for you Call use_phw_ggplot() and use_phw_flextable() in the setup chunk
Needs The rmarkdown package; LaTeX for PDF Quarto 1.5 or later (recent versions of RStudio include it)

phw_setup_check() tells you whether Pandoc, Quarto and LaTeX are available on your computer.

R Markdown

Put a phwstyle format in the YAML header, and knit as usual:

---
title: "Report title"
author: "Team name"
output: phwstyle::phw_word_document
---
Format Output
phwstyle::phw_html_document A web page with the header band, a floating table of contents and the PHW Bootstrap theme. Works offline: the fonts are inside the file
phwstyle::phw_word_document A Word document built from the PHW reference document: Ubuntu, navy headings, tables with horizontal rules only, a header band and a page footer
phwstyle::phw_pdf_document A PDF through LaTeX (XeLaTeX), with a full-page cover, a running header band and a footer

To start from a working example in RStudio, choose File > New File > R Markdown > From Template > PHW report. It knits to all three formats.

The formats call use_phw_ggplot() and use_phw_flextable() before knitting, so don’t repeat them in the document. Add theme_phw() or a PHW scale to a plot only to change something for that plot.

Options go under the format name. Each format takes the arguments of the R Markdown format it builds on, and these ones too:

output:
  phwstyle::phw_pdf_document:
    toc: true
    team: "Team name"
    number_sections: false
    fig_width: 7
    palette: accessible
  • toc and number_sections add a table of contents and numbered headings. The HTML format turns on the table of contents, the PDF format turns on numbered headings, and the Word format turns on neither.
  • fig_width and fig_height set the default figure size in inches.
  • team adds a team line to the PDF cover, and cover: false drops the cover.
  • style_plots: false stops the format calling use_phw_ggplot() and use_phw_flextable(), for a document that styles its own charts.
  • palette picks the colours for the whole document. See Default and accessible colours.

?phw_formats lists every option.

To render from R without a YAML header, pass the format object with the same options:

rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", phwstyle::phw_html_document(toc = FALSE))
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", phwstyle::phw_pdf_document(team = "Team name"))

Quarto

Run this once in your project folder. It adds the PHW extension in _extensions/phw and writes a starter report:

phwstyle::use_phw_quarto(template = "report")

template = "slides" and template = "dashboard" write a starter presentation or dashboard instead, and template = "none" adds only the extension. Run it again with overwrite = TRUE after updating phwstyle, to pick up changes to the extension.

Then name the format in the YAML header:

---
title: "Report title"
format: phw-docx
---
Format Output
phw-html A web page with the header band and a table of contents
phw-docx A Word document built from the PHW reference document
phw-pptx PowerPoint slides built from the PHW template: 16:9, Ubuntu text and navy titles
phw-typst A PDF through Typst, which comes with Quarto, so no LaTeX is needed. Cover page, running header band, page numbers
phw-pdf A PDF through LaTeX, for teams that already use it
phw-revealjs 16:9 HTML slides with a title slide, logo and footer
phw-dashboard A one-page dashboard with a navy navigation bar and PHW cards

A Quarto extension styles the page but can’t run R code, so style the charts and tables in the setup chunk, as the starter documents do:


``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(phwstyle)
use_phw_ggplot()
use_phw_flextable()
```

The Typst PDF takes a few extra options in the YAML header: phw-team: "Team name" adds a team line to the cover, phw-no-cover: true drops the cover, and phw-org, phw-page-label and phw-of-label change the footer wording. See ?use_phw_quarto.

Quarto builds a phw-pptx deck from your headings and content. To fill a deck from R, with a slide for each chart or table, see Excel, PowerPoint and Word.

To make several formats from one document, list them:

format:
  phw-html: default
  phw-docx: default
  phw-typst: default

The gallery shows every format, including the slides and dashboard.

Default and accessible colours

Some readers need colours that stay distinct for every type of colour blindness. The accessible palette does that, and switching it on for a document changes every chart, table and widget made with phwstyle (see Colours and accessibility).

To switch a document for good, add one line to its YAML header. It works the same in R Markdown and Quarto:

phw-palette: accessible

To make both versions from one unchanged document, set the palette when you render. In R Markdown, use output_options:

word <- "phwstyle::phw_word_document"
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report.docx")
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", word, output_file = "report-accessible.docx",
                  output_options = list(palette = "accessible"))

In Quarto, set the environment variable PHWSTYLE_PALETTE for the second render. From R (this works on Windows too):

system2("quarto", c("render", "report.qmd", "--to", "phw-docx"))

Sys.setenv(PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible")
system2("quarto", c("render", "report.qmd", "--to", "phw-docx",
                    "-o", "report-accessible.docx"))
Sys.unsetenv("PHWSTYLE_PALETTE")

Or from a terminal:

quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx
PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx -o report-accessible.docx

In PowerShell, set it with $env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible" before the second render, and clear it with Remove-Item Env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE afterwards.

The setting has to reach R through the document or the environment: Quarto doesn’t pass -M values or _quarto.yml settings on to R.

If you keep colour keys in a file (phw_key_file() in the setup chunk), each group keeps its colour in both versions, from one run to the next.

The files behind the formats

Three functions write the files the formats are built from. Use them to look at what a format does, or to brand a tool that phwstyle has no format for. Each takes a file path and returns it.

  • phw_reference_docx() writes the Word document behind phw_word_document() and phw-docx. Open it in Word to see its styles, or pass it to Quarto as reference-doc or to officer::read_docx().
  • phw_reference_pptx() writes the PowerPoint template behind phw_pptx() and phw-pptx. It has one slide master called "PHW" and the layouts that Excel, PowerPoint and Word describes.
  • phw_latex_header() writes the LaTeX header behind phw_pdf_document(), with the font and logo paths filled in. team adds the cover line and cover = FALSE drops the cover. Use it for another LaTeX format, such as bookdown.
library(phwstyle)
files <- c(docx = phw_reference_docx(),
           pptx = phw_reference_pptx(),
           tex = phw_latex_header(team = "Team name"))
file.exists(files)
#> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE

Give each function a file to keep the copy, and name it in your document:

format:
  docx:
    reference-doc: phw-reference.docx
  pdf:
    include-in-header: phw-header.tex

Fonts and the logo

HTML pages, slides and dashboards embed Ubuntu, and the PDF formats use the copy inside phwstyle. Word and PowerPoint files name Ubuntu without embedding it, so they show it only on computers that have it. See Installation and setup for installing the fonts, and the logos section for adding the PHW logo. After adding the logo, run use_phw_quarto(overwrite = TRUE) so the Quarto extension picks it up.
